messages:
LynxBay Support: Hey, on behalf of @LynxBay ops — we've had p99 spikes on the /v1/embeddings endpoint starting ~2026-03-12T14:00Z. Their app experiences 504s and long tails. Metrics they sent: p50=38ms, p95=250ms, p99=1.9s (baseline p99 ~220ms). Tenant: lynxbay-prod. No deploys on their side. Can SRE take a look?

Priya - Customer Success: Thanks for the ping — opening a case with them now and asking for request IDs + a repro curl. tagging @Eli.

Eli (SRE): On it. Quick checklist while we wait: 1) attach a sample X-Request-Id from a slow request, 2) repro curl (include X-Redwood-Tenant header), 3) any client IPs. Also whether this is embeddings-only or generation too.

LynxBay Support: attaching a minimal repro curl that hits the slow path (they said embeddings heavy).
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: lynxbay-prod" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large-v1","input":["test"],"top_k":1}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings?stream=false
```
Response sometimes returns 504 or takes >1.5s. One sample header they sent: X-Request-Id: rQ2k9b-20260312-xx

Jordan (Eng-Platform): I see concurrent queue wait spikes on a handful of nodes ~14:02-14:25Z. Host group cg-prod-gpu-7 had queue_waits clustering around 700–1800ms. Could be a noisy tenant scheduling onto same hosts or a disk I/O issue on local cache. Pulling runtime logs.

Eli (SRE): Can you paste the runtime tail? I want to see KV cache hits / misses and any long kernel times.

Jordan (Eng-Platform): Pasting excerpt from runtime log around the times (stripped PII):
```text
2026-03-12T14:05:11Z host=cg-prod-gpu-7 req=rQ2k9b queue_wait=1462ms exec_time=28ms kv_cache_hit=false model=embed-large-v1
2026-03-12T14:05:12Z host=cg-prod-gpu-7 req=rQ2k9c queue_wait=1510ms exec_time=24ms kv_cache_hit=false model=embed-large-v1
2026-03-12T14:05:30Z host=cg-prod-gpu-7 req=rQ2k9d queue_wait=1720ms exec_time=30ms kv_cache_hit=false model=embed-large-v1
```
Looks like queue_wait is dominating. Also noticing a burst of other tenant requests coming from several high-rate IPs.

rate-limiter-bot: action=throttle tenant=lynxbay-prod previous_rate=120r/s new_rate=60r/s reason="protect-host-stability"

Eli (SRE): That throttle is auto-applied when host qlen goes > 100 and tenant has no reservation. Good for host stability but increases tail for clients that need sustained throughput. Two hypotheses: 1) noisy neighbor (another tenant saturated the shared pool), 2) our routing sent lynxbay to a smaller host with degraded disk/cache.

Infra Ops: Confirming — a tenant we onboarded yesterday started a heavy embedding job around 14:00 and saturated the same availability pool. We're seeing high blkio wait on cg-prod-gpu-7 for the period.

LynxBay Support: Customer is asking for a fast mitigation — they can’t ship to users with these tails. What quick actions can we do without full Dedicated?

Eli (SRE): Quick mitigations (short-lived):
- Add lynxbay-prod to a temporary allowlist that gives them reservation on 2 workers (bypass shared queue).
- Increase their per-tenant rate cap slightly while we stabilize (e.g., 60->100r/s), with strict burst shaping.
- Reroute new requests away from cg-prod-gpu-7 via routing override.
- If disk/block I/O is the culprit, restart node after draining or move cached shards.

Jordan (Eng-Platform): I can create a routing override. Example admin API call (infra only):
```bash
curl -X PUT -H "Authorization: Bearer infra_token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://internal.redwood.ai/v1/admin/tenants/lynxbay-prod/route \
  -d '{"target_pool":"reserved-small-2","reason":"customer tail mitigation 2026-03-12"}'
```
This will move new requests to reserved-small-2 within ~30s. Existing in-flight requests stay on old host.

Eli (SRE): I applied a temporary allowlist + 2-worker reservation and bumped rate cap to 90r/s for lynxbay-prod at 14:18Z. Also initiated a soft-drain of cg-prod-gpu-7 to migrate noisy tenant work.

LynxBay Support: After the change they report p99 dropped to ~260ms within 90s. No more 504s. Customer very appreciative.

kimberly (Acct Exec): Looping in sales — we should discuss Dedicated / reserved capacity options with LynxBay; they are a good fit.

Priya - Customer Success: Action items: 1) Confirm with customer that tails cleared and get log of any remaining errors. 2) Schedule post-mortem with Eng-Platform and Infra Ops to identify why noisy tenant landed on same pool. 3) Offer migration path to Dedicated or reservation plan.

Eli (SRE): Post-mortem notes (short): root cause = aggressive embedding batch job from a recently onboarded tenant landed in same availability pool; autoscaler didn't detect sustained load quickly enough; per-tenant assignment lacked a minimum reservation for new high-throughput tenants. Mitigations: tighten new-tenant heuristics, add an automated slow-roll reservation if sustained r/s > 50 for > 5 minutes, and improve blkio alerting on host pools.

Infra Ops: We'll also add a temporary alert rule: if queue_wait 95th > 500ms on a host and blkio util > 70% -> escalate to SRE and mark pool as degraded for routing.

LynxBay Support: Customer accepted mitigation and wants a follow-up in 48h. We'll keep the reservation for 24h while they test. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Eli (SRE): Marking this thread resolved for now. Will attach post-mortem doc once we have one.
